results.title: Scores Overview – Apollo
results.content: # Scores Overview. When you use scores based on the attributes that define your ideal customers, you can more easily identify the prospects likely to convert into buyers. Apollo generates auto-scores based on your company website and prospecting activity. These scores are based on signals that contribute to a rating for a prospect. Apollo uses auto-scores by default when you search for people or companies. Apollo automatically generates scores based on your account and prospecting activity, helping identify and rank the most important business scenarios affecting your ideal customers. When you save contacts and accounts, Apollo learns more about the ideal customer profile for your organization, and over time, auto-scores become more refined to match your team's outreach. Apollo generates each person or company score based on how well they match signals within a score. With auto-scores, Apollo automatically selects signals based on your organization and its prospecting activity. Apollo then assigns people and companies individual ratings based on how well they match signals in the score. Apollo assigns one of the following ratings to each person or company that you prospect based on how well they fit your score:. Apollo enables auto-score by default when you prospect for people and companies in Apollo. Apollo shares the score rating and the signals that contributed to the rating. Apollo generates auto-scores for your team based on 2 main sources of information:. Apollo assigns people and companies individual score ratings based on how well they match your score. For example, if a company matches 2 good signals and 1 excellent signal, the company would receive an excellent score rating. When you search for people or companies, Apollo shares a score rating for each result. To use scores when prospecting, upgrade your plan. If you use a CRM like Salesforce or HubSpot, Apollo syncs scores for contacts and accounts with your CRM:. The legacy scoring model was based on points, with each prospect earning points for matching signals in a score. The new scoring model is based on each prospect earning a score for the highest performing signal the prospect matches.

Apollo.io automates sales processes on top of that, providing AI insights meant to accelerate deals and optimize sales funnels. [...] ## Apollo.io Database

Apollo.io’s database centers on B2B contacts. Verified emails and direct-dial phone numbers, plus job titles, make up the core fields. Apollo.io sources this from public records and its own proprietary methods to maximize coverage.

results.title: Apollo.io Review 2026: Pricing, Features, Pros & Cons | SalesHive
results.content: Apollo.io is an AI-powered sales intelligence and engagement platform that helps B2B revenue teams find and engage leads, automate outreach, manage deals, and enrich CRM data in a single workspace. At its core is a continuously updated B2B database of more than 210 million contacts and 35 million companies, paired with advanced search, intent data, and workflow automation so teams can build pipeline faster and with more precision. [...] Apollo.io is an AI-powered sales intelligence and engagement platform that combines a large, continuously updated B2B contact database with tools for prospecting, data enrichment, multichannel outreach, and revenue analytics. Sales and marketing teams use Apollo.io to discover ideal buyers, enrich CRM records, run email and call sequences, book meetings, and track performance in one unified workspace. [...] Compared with legacy data providers like ZoomInfo, Apollo.io generally offers a smaller but still substantial and fast-growing database at a much lower price point, especially for small and mid-sized teams. Where ZoomInfo often needs to be paired with a separate engagement platform, Apollo bundles data, enrichment, sequencing, and dialer capabilities into a single subscription, which can significantly reduce stack complexity and cost.

results.title: Apollo News, Junge Freiheit journalists attacked while covering protests in Germany - Committee to Protect Journalists
results.content:
Three reporters working for news website Apollo News— Jonas Aston, Marius Marx, and a third whose name the outlet did not disclose — needed medical treatment after being chased, hit, kicked, and pelted with objects while documenting the protests outside the July 4 conference. They were taken by police to an ambulance, and Aston was later treated in hospital for a head wound. [...] Apollo News reporters 

Three Apollo News reporters were chased and attacked while covering protests against the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party during its annual conference in Erfurt, eastern Germany, on July 4, 2026. A Junge Freiheit reporter was also attacked. (Screenshot: Welt/YouTube)

# Apollo News, Junge Freiheit journalists attacked while covering protests in Germany

### Share this: [...] Police said they were investigating the Apollo News attack as suspected dangerous bodily harm, with three journalists listed as victims, two of whom suffered minor injuries. They were also investigating the Junge Freiheit incident as a robbery and bodily harm, involving three suspects. State police said Erfurt criminal police had formed a working group to prioritize all offenses linked to the weekend protest and were reviewing photo and video evidence.
